title: Ramayana Becomes First Hindi Film to Net Rs 100 Crore From South Dubbed Versions
excerpt: Six days into its run, the Nitesh Tiwari epic has collected Rs 104.45 crore net in India from its Kannada, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam versions alone, passing the lifetime South dubbed totals of Dhurandhar 2, War 2, Jawan and Animal, according to Sacnilk tracking.
body:
• Ramayana has become the first Hindi-origin film to cross Rs 100 crore India net from South Indian dubbed versions, reaching Rs 104.45 crore in six days, according to Sacnilk.
  • Kannada is the biggest contributor at Rs 41.20 crore net, followed by Telugu (Rs 33 crore), Tamil (Rs 17.35 crore) and Malayalam (Rs 12.90 crore).
  • The dubbed versions account for about 23.7% of the film's Rs 440.45 crore India net total through day six.
  • The six-day dubbed total already exceeds the lifetime South dubbed collections of Dhurandhar 2 (Rs 68.54 crore), War 2 (Rs 58.96 crore), Jawan (Rs 57.94 crore) and Animal (Rs 50.89 crore).

Ramayana has set a box-office record no Hindi film has managed before. Six days into its theatrical run, the film has collected Rs 104.45 crore net in India from its South Indian dubbed versions alone, becoming the first Hindi-origin production to cross Rs 100 crore from dubbed releases in the South, according to Sacnilk's tracking. The figures are trade estimates compiled by the tracker, not certified studio accounts.

The film, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi. It was made in Hindi and released across India with dubbed versions in Kannada, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam.

"Telugu follows at Rs 33 crore net, with Tamil at Rs 17.35 crore and Malayalam at Rs 12.90 crore."

Kannada Leads the Dubbed Run

Kannada is the strongest of the four dubbed versions at Rs 41.20 crore net, a performance Sacnilk links in part to Yash's popularity in Karnataka. Telugu follows at Rs 33 crore net, with Tamil at Rs 17.35 crore and Malayalam at Rs 12.90 crore. Pinkvilla reported the dubbed versions have grossed about Rs 125 crore in six days, and that in Kerala the film grossed Rs 20 crore in six days, passing the lifetime Kerala totals of Dhurandhar: The Revenge (Rs 19.50 crore), Jawan (Rs 13.40 crore) and Pathaan (Rs 13.10 crore).

Sacnilk also reported the film has become the highest-grossing Bollywood film in Karnataka and Kerala. The dubbed versions contributed about 23.7% of the film's Rs 440.45 crore India net collection through day six, according to the tracker.

Past the Lifetime Totals of Bigger-Earning Rivals

The comparison that gives the record its weight is against completed runs. Dhurandhar 2 collected Rs 68.54 crore net from South dubbed versions over its entire theatrical run; War 2 collected Rs 58.96 crore, Jawan Rs 57.94 crore and Animal Rs 50.89 crore, according to Sacnilk's table. Ramayana passed all four in six days, exceeding Dhurandhar 2's lifetime South dubbed total by more than half.

One distinction matters. Adipurush collected more than Rs 130 crore net in Telugu alone, but it was produced as a Hindi-Telugu bilingual, so its Telugu earnings are not classified as dubbed-language collections. Excluding Telugu, its Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam versions together contributed about Rs 6.95 crore net, according to Sacnilk.

What It Means for Hindi Cinema's Southern Bet

Hindi films have traditionally earned little from South Indian dubbed versions. Ramayana's release model was different: according to 123Telugu, the dubbed versions were given a large show count in Hyderabad and Bengaluru, unlike the token releases Hindi films usually receive in those markets. The result suggests the ceiling was a distribution choice as much as an audience limit.

Worldwide, Sacnilk's tracker puts the film at about Rs 823.50 crore gross after six days, comprising Rs 526.50 crore India gross and an estimated Rs 297 crore overseas, with the overseas figures described as preliminary. For diaspora audiences, the film is playing in its original Hindi and in dubbed versions, and its overseas run is now part of the same record-setting pattern seen at home.

With the Bhai Dooj holiday still to come in its first week, the South dubbed total is expected to rise further, according to Sacnilk. The next benchmark in the tracker's coverage is Dhurandhar 2's Rs 1,813.39 crore lifetime worldwide gross, of which Ramayana has reached roughly 45% in six days.
